content: Written 2026-10-07 22:15, before the proxy and before any formal run. DN = a switch (--depth-normalized, off = GaME as published) on GaME's depth term in row 4's backend. User 21:56: 'yes, we certainly give ourselves the advantage' to the question of a switchable correction of GaME's depth fit (rows 1/3 not rerun). The export readout (median) and the evaluation are unchanged.

GaME's loss fits the unnormalised D = sum z alpha T (flashsplat forward.cu:395 'D += depths[global_id] * alpha * T;', game.py depth_loss = l1(depth, gt_depth)); the official export reads the median (T first below 0.5). Measured on B's keyframes (GT-free, analysis/depth_bias_s3cb_b.json, far_bias_s3cb_b.json): 7.9 % of pixels render > 5 cm deeper than the reading (1.9 % at 0.5-1.5 m up to 35.3 % at 3.5-5 m); in that subset median - d 6.6-7.3 cm, D/alpha - d 5.8-7.3 cm, median - D/alpha 0.2-1.1 cm, D - d 1.73 cm, alpha 0.985, d(1/alpha - 1) 4.4 cm: with alpha < 1 a fit of D leaves the surface d(1/alpha - 1) deeper. Note: the subset is selected by the outcome (the failing pixels), so the decomposition is not a causal proof; the proxy G1 decides. Source of the normalised depth: 2DGS gaussian_renderer/__init__.py (original checked): 'render_depth_expected = allmap[0:1]; render_depth_expected = (render_depth_expected / render_alpha); render_depth_expected = torch.nan_to_num(render_depth_expected, 0, 0)' and 'surf_depth = render_depth_expected * (1-pipe.depth_ratio) + (pipe.depth_ratio) * render_depth_median'. Not explained: the 2.3 % of pixels rendered > 5 cm nearer (alpha 1.0).
visible pixel: alpha >= GaME's min_opacity 0.3 (flat.yaml: 'minimum Gaussian alpha to be considered visible'; game.py uses it in the same role); alpha taken as a constant of the step; no new number.

From real_row4s3cb/checkpoint_b.pt (keyframes restored): two arms with identical keyframe set (B's, S3), iteration count (50 x B keyframes), random seeds (python/numpy/torch 0): control = GaME's loss, DN = the new term; each exported as tsdf_export does (map at B's end, all keyframes, median) and scored with the official scorer (3d_vsg python). Gate: DN - control official G1 F1 >= +0.3 -> formal chain; also read (GT-free) the share of B keyframe pixels with median > d + 5 cm in both arms. G8 is computed only for the dataset's last session (held-out frames in C), so the B proxy has no G8; G8 is read in the formal chain's C with both depth readouts (D and D/alpha) reported.
When adopted: on for A, B and C (and synthetic), not for B alone.
two arms ~10-15 min each (one process each), no checkpoints written (export inline).
the deeper-than-5-cm share falls in the DN arm; official G1 gain unknown (the proxy is conservative: the map was trained with the old loss, a fine-tune of equal length only partly changes it).

(a) the arms run one after the other (GPU/RAM: the synthetic A run is on the GPU); (b) read also the alpha distribution in both arms (pixels with alpha < 0.9, < 0.5, and without a median) -- the unnormalised D term pushes alpha towards 1 implicitly, DN on visible pixels leaves only the colour term to do it; (c) assumption: alpha is a constant of the step (detached), unlike 2DGS's fully differentiable render_depth_expected / render_alpha; if the proxy gains, a non-detached variant may be compared before the formal chain. 2DGS sec. 4 (supervisor checked the original): 'It is important to normalize the depth with the accumulated alpha A = sum w_i'.

GATE FAILED (detached alpha): control 91.30/92.97/92.13, DN 60.95/75.21/67.34 (official scorer); GT-free in the DN arm: alpha < 0.9 on 52.8 % of B keyframe pixels, alpha < 0.5 (no median) 41.8 %, rendered > 5 cm nearer 42.7 % (control: deeper 9.35 %, nearer 1.17 %). Cause by construction: with alpha a constant of the step, |D/alpha - d| is lowered by lowering every opacity on the ray (D shrinks, alpha does not follow), so the term drives opacity down -- the detach was my implementation choice, not the 2DGS form (render_depth_expected / render_alpha is differentiable in both). The detached form is withdrawn.

Rule from now (user 22:4x: code that runs must not carry bugs): before any GPU run (1) the source formula next to the code, every deviation listed with its reason; (2) a small numeric check of the properties the formula has; (3) a short smoke reading the key internal quantities. For DN2: (2) done, analysis/alpha_grad_check.json: FlashSplat's backward vs central finite differences on the raw opacities of 20 Gaussians of one real B keyframe -- alpha: sign agreement 1.0, relative error median 0.10 (q90 0.30); D/alpha: sign 1.0, rel. error median 0.044 (q90 0.28); scaling every opacity by 0.99 changes D/alpha by 0.12 cm (median). (3) smoke queued (20 B keyframes, 300 iterations, alpha < 0.5 / < 0.9 shares every 50), stop rule fixed before the numbers: DN2's alpha < 0.5 share > control + 1 pp at the end or rising monotonically -> no full arm. Supervisor's prediction written down before: GaME's colour loss has a black background, so dark surfaces may lose alpha at little colour cost while D/alpha is scale-invariant.

The smoke is a one-way gate: a collapse stops, but passing it is not a conclusion -- it gives each keyframe ~15 iterations against the full arm's 50 per keyframe, so a slow drift of alpha may not show in 300 iterations. After the full arm, the alpha < 0.5 share (dn_proxy.py reports it) is read before the official G1.
